title: The 1886 Charleston, South Carolina, earthquake - a 1986 perspective
citation: Nuttli, O.W., Bollinger, G.A., and Herrmann, R.B., 1986, The 1886 Charleston, South Carolina, earthquake - a 1986 perspective: U.S. Geological Survey Circular 985, map scale 1:338,000.
notes:
Seismological circular on the 1886 Charleston earthquake; mostly intensity and ground-motion discussion (not recorded). Recorded: Coastal Plain sediment thickness, the inferred epicenter, and faults/focal mechanisms discussed in Chapter 2. Pages are two-column text interleaved line by line, so quotes are short single-column fragments. Felt-intensity reports, building damage and predicted ground motions were not recorded (not geologic values). Talwani (1982) also reports an abrupt P-wave velocity increase at about 6 miles depth (p.25), not recorded.
Pages 47-64: remaining felt reports (not recorded), concluding remarks with fault and paleoliquefaction findings cited from other studies, references, and the magnitude/intensity appendix (not recorded). References on general seismology outside South Carolina (Ayers, Campbell, Coffman, Dowding, Lawson, Nuttli 1983/1979/1984 Mississippi valley, Ramelli, Richter, Singh, Tilford) were skipped. Two-column text is interleaved, so quotes are single-column fragments.
